newsitem.title: GHANA: Foreign investors take major stake in Ghana bank.
newsitem.headline: Foreign investors take major stake in Ghana bank.

text.p: A consortium of foreign investors took a controlling 51 percent stake in Ghana's Social Security Bank on Friday, adding an 11 percent stake to the 40 percent share it bought in February, the Ghana Stock Exchange said.

British company Blakeney Management Limited leads the consortium which also includes Morgan Stanley Asset Management, Alliance Capital Management, J P Morgan Investment Management and New Africa Investors.
An exchange statement said the consortium was the first to invest in Ghana in this way since the opening of the exchange to foreign investors in 1993.
The move helped boost turnover on the Ghana Stock Exchange to 7,877,700 shares traded compared to 39,850 on Wednesday. The bank accounted for 7,837,600 of the total.

The Bank was listed on the exchange in October 1995 when 21 percent of its stock was sold to the public at 800 cedis a share. The Blakeney-led consortium bought a strategic 40-percent stake in February, concluding the privatisation of the bank.
The bank's 1996 after-tax profit was 26 billion cedis, up from 16 billion cedis in 1995.
The value of the bank's shares rose four cedis on Friday to 1,254 cedis.
